answer: To register extra identities, an attacker must acquire and attest separate kernels, each requiring a costly jade-signed credential issued once per device by a trusted registrar, so forging N identities costs N times the stake plus credential fees. Sybil resistance can use a bonded provenance anchor: each agent locks a stake tied to a verified hardware kernel attestation, and that bond is the anchor for its identity across epochs. In practice, Agent0102 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
